classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the symbolic discriminant as a perfect square, connect it to rationality through the quadratic formula, and solve separately when the quadratic term vanishes.

content.prompt: Show that $(p-3)x^2+6x-(p+3)=0$ has only rational roots for every integer value of $p$.

answer.short: Every root is rational. For $p\ne3$, $\Delta=(2p)^2$ is a perfect square. For $p=3$, the equation is linear with root $x=1$.
answer.worked:
If $p\ne3$, the equation is quadratic.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=6^2-4(p-3)(-p-3)\\\Delta&=36+4(p^2-9)\\\Delta&=(2p)^2\end{align*}$$

For integer $p$, $\sqrt{\Delta}=2|p|$ is an integer. The quadratic formula gives $x=\frac{-6\pm2|p|}{2(p-3)}$, so each root is rational. If $p=3$, the equation becomes $6x-6=0$, which has the rational root $x=1$.
